landing.title: The idea doesn't have to stay an idea.
landing.subtitle: Ventrio turns a hobby, a skill, a problem, or a half-formed idea into a real, working first version — built the moment you describe it.
landing.composerPlaceholder: Describe a hobby, skill, idea, or problem…
landing.explainerSubtitle: What happens between your first sentence and a real project.
landing.explainerStep1Body: Describe a hobby, skill, problem, or half-formed idea.
landing.explainerStep2Body: Ventrio turns it into a polished first version you can shape.
landing.explainerStep3Body: Structure, hierarchy, and details settle into something ready to publish.
landing.evolveTitle: From a sentence to something people can open.
landing.evolveSubtitle: Ventrio builds the first working version and puts it on a real address.
landing.evolveStep1Body: Say what you want in your own words. Ventrio works out a direction with you.
landing.evolveStep2Body: Not a mockup — a real application you can open, click through, and read.
landing.evolveStep3Body: One action puts it on a public link you can send to anyone.
landing.improveSubtitle: Don't just build websites — develop products. Every step is yours to direct.
landing.improve1Body: A hobby, a skill, a problem, or a half-formed thought is enough to begin.
landing.improve2Body: Ventrio proposes concrete directions. Pick one, or ask it to sharpen the one you like.
landing.improve3Body: An application, a dashboard, a tool, a store, a landing page — you decide the shape.
landing.improve4Body: Ventrio builds a real first version and opens it in the preview beside the conversation.
landing.improve5Body: Put it on a public link and share it with the people it is for.
landing.composerPlaceholderFinal: Describe what you want to create…
landing.heroLede: Describe what you want. Ventrio builds it, puts it online, and keeps working on it with you — by talking, not by learning a dashboard.
landing.heroNote: Free to start. No card needed.
landing.loopLede: Most AI builders hand you a result and stop there. Ventrio stays in the conversation after launch, so the thing you made can keep changing without you starting over.
landing.loop1Body: Say what you want in your own words.
landing.loop2Body: It gets a real web address of its own.
landing.loop3Body: Ask for a change the way you'd ask a person.
landing.loop4Body: The live version updates. No rebuild.
landing.loop5Body: See what people actually did with it.
landing.whyTitle: Not a builder that hands you a file
landing.whyLede: A one-shot generator is finished the moment it answers. The hard part starts after that — and it is the part Ventrio is built for.
landing.why1: It doesn't stop at version one
landing.why1Body: The first result is a starting point you can keep changing by asking, not a download you are stuck with.
landing.why2Body: A price, a headline, a whole section — say what should be different and it changes.
landing.why3Body: Every conversation is about this project, so you never explain what you're building twice.
landing.why4: You can see it the whole time
landing.why4Body: The preview beside the conversation is the real thing running, not a picture of it.
landing.afterLede: This is the part that usually needs a developer, a dashboard, or a rebuild. Here it is a message.
landing.after1Body: Rewrite a headline, a button, a whole page — ask, and the live version updates.
landing.after2Body: Add a section, a form, another page. The structure is not frozen after launch.
landing.after3Body: Responses people send through your published project, collected and counted for you.
landing.after4Body: Pick the conversation back up later and carry on where you left it.
landing.demoYou: make the headline shorter and add a sign-up form
landing.demoV: Done — the headline is two words shorter and there's a form under it. Want the form to email you each time?
landing.chatLede: We're building Ventrio into the places you already type: Telegram and WhatsApp, with text, voice notes, screenshots and short commands. It is not available yet — everything above works on the web today.
landing.priceTitleEm: Pay when it's carrying something real.
landing.priceLede: Every plan builds and publishes the same way. The limits are the only difference.
landing.faq1: Do I need to know how to code?
landing.faq1Body: No. You describe what you want in ordinary language, and you change it the same way afterwards.
landing.faq2Body: A page, a small site, or a working app — a sign-up page, a booking form, a study tool, a directory. If you can describe it, it is worth trying.
landing.faq3Body: Yes. Publishing gives your project its own web address and keeps it there until you unpublish it.
landing.faq4: What happens to what I make?
landing.faq4Body: It is yours. Ventrio hosts it and you can take it offline whenever you want.
landing.faq5: Is it really free to start?
landing.faq5Body: Yes, and no card is asked for. The free plan builds three projects a month and keeps one of them online.
landing.faq6: Can I use it in Russian?
landing.faq6Body: Yes. Ventrio talks in the language you write in, and your project is built in that language too.
landing.closeTitle: What do you want to make?
landing.closeLede: Say it in a sentence. You'll have something real to look at in a few minutes.
landing.demoWordsBefore: Saturday chess for people who have never played
landing.demoWordsSub: Cafés and parks around the city. No clocks, no pressure.
landing.demoDeviceNote: The preview in the workspace is the running project, at whatever width you ask for.
landing.demoFeedbackNote: Example figures. Ventrio counts responses people send through your published project — it does not track visitors.
landing.demoAnywhereNote: Messenger access is not available yet. Everything else here works on the web today.

info.aboutTitle: Turn what you care about into a real project.
info.aboutP1: Most tools ask you to arrive with a finished plan. Ventrio starts from wherever you actually are — a hobby, a skill, a problem you keep noticing, or a half-formed idea.
info.aboutP2: You describe it in your own words. Ventrio understands what matters, shapes a realistic direction, and builds a first version you can actually use — not a roadmap or a list of homework.
info.aboutP3: From there you keep changing it, publish it, hear from real people, and improve it. That loop is the whole point.
info.whoTitle: For anyone with something they care about.
info.whoIntro: You don't need to be a founder, a designer, or a developer. You need one honest starting point.
info.who1Body: Turn the thing you love doing into something other people can find, join, or follow.
info.who2Body: Shape what you're good at into a way to help someone specific.
info.who3Body: Take something that frustrates you and make a first version that helps others with it.
info.who4Body: Give the idea you can't stop thinking about a real place to live and be tested.
info.faqQ1: Do I need a startup idea?
info.faqA1: No. A hobby, skill, problem, or rough interest is enough. Ventrio helps you find the project inside it.
info.faqA2: A real, editable first version of your project — with its own name, copy, and structure — not advice or a plan.
info.faqA3: Yes. You keep talking to Ventrio to reshape the idea, audience, copy, or format, then publish when it's ready.
info.faqA4: Publish your project and share one clear link. What people tell you is yours to read, and you decide what the next version should be.
info.faqA5: You can start creating right away. Just describe something you care about and go from there.

privacy.intro: This policy explains what data {productName} collects, why, and who processes it. {productName} is operated by {operatorName}, {operatorCountry}{operatorCityPart}. Questions: {contactEmail}.

sections.title: What we collect
sections.body:
• Account information — the email address you sign up with, and an encrypted password. Authentication is handled by Supabase.
• What you write — the ideas, descriptions and messages you send to {productName}, and the conversations they belong to.
• What {productName} builds for you — the directions proposed for your project, the generated application or site, and the versions you publish.
• Usage counters — how many generations and idea conversations you have used against your free allowance.
• Technical logs — request logs kept by our hosting providers, which include IP address, browser user agent, and timestamps.

We do not collect analytics about how visitors behave on the products you publish. No such tracking exists in {productName}.

sections.title: Why we use it
sections.body: To create and secure your account; to generate, store and display the projects you ask for; to publish a project when you choose to; to enforce free-usage limits fairly; to keep the service running and to investigate faults and abuse.

sections.title: AI processing
sections.body:
Generating a direction or a first version requires sending your idea, your project description and the related conversation to a third-party AI provider. {productName} currently uses Google (Gemini API) for idea conversations and for generating applications, and Anthropic for parts of the in-project assistant and feedback analysis.

Those providers process this content to return a result. We do not control their internal handling and we do not send them your email address or password. If you would rather a piece of information were not sent to an AI provider, do not put it in a prompt or a project.

sections.title: Who else processes your data
sections.body:
• Supabase — accounts, authentication and the database where projects, conversations and published versions are stored.
• Vercel — hosting for the website and its server functions, including request logs.
• Railway — hosting for the background service that generates applications.
• Google and Anthropic — AI processing, as described above.

We do not sell your data, and we do not share it for advertising.

sections.title: Where data is processed
sections.body: These providers operate infrastructure in several countries, so your data may be processed outside the country you live in. We choose providers that offer standard contractual protections for such transfers.

sections.title: How long we keep it
sections.body: Projects, conversations and generated versions are kept while your account exists, so you can come back to them. Technical logs are kept for a short period by our hosting providers under their own retention settings. When you delete your account, your projects, conversations and published versions are deleted with it.

sections.title: Published projects are public
sections.body: When you publish a project it becomes available at a public address that anyone with the link can open. Nothing else about your account becomes public. You can unpublish at any time from the project's preview toolbar.

sections.title: Security
sections.body: Access to your data is restricted per account at the database level. Passwords are stored hashed by Supabase and are never visible to us. No system is perfectly secure, and we do not claim otherwise.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You can access and correct your account details, export or delete your projects, and delete your account entirely from the Delete Account page. Depending on where you live you may also have the right to object to processing or to lodge a complaint with a data protection authority. Write to {contactEmail}.

sections.title: Minors
sections.body: {productName} is not intended for children under {minimumAge}. If we learn that an account belongs to someone younger, we will delete it.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: If this policy changes materially we will update the effective date below and, where the change is significant, tell account holders by email.

terms.intro: By using {productName} (the "Service") you agree to these terms. The Service is operated by {operatorName}, {operatorCountry}{operatorCityPart}.

sections.title: What the Service does
sections.body: {productName} helps you turn an idea into a working first version of a website or application. You describe an idea, {productName} proposes directions with you, generates a first version, shows it in a preview, and lets you publish it at a public address.

sections.title: Your account
sections.body: You need an account to use the Service. Keep your credentials to yourself; you are responsible for what happens under your account. You must be at least {minimumAge} years old.

sections.title: What you may not do
sections.body: Do not use the Service to create or publish anything unlawful, deceptive, or infringing; anything that impersonates a real person or organisation; malware, phishing or credential-harvesting pages; or content that harasses or endangers others. Do not attempt to break out of the preview sandbox, disrupt the Service, or work around usage limits.

sections.title: Your content and what you make
sections.body:
You keep ownership of what you write and of the projects generated for you. You grant {productName} the permissions it needs to store, process and display them in order to run the Service — including sending them to the AI providers named in the Privacy Policy.

You are responsible for what you publish. AI-generated output is not checked by a human before you see it, and publishing it is your decision.

sections.title: Generated output is not unique
sections.body: Similar prompts can produce similar results for different people. {productName} does not promise that anything generated for you is original, or that it does not resemble output produced for someone else.

sections.title: Usage limits
sections.body: Free accounts have a daily allowance for generations and idea conversations. We may change these allowances. A generation that fails through no fault of yours is refunded to your allowance.

sections.title: Availability
sections.body: The Service is provided as it is, without a guaranteed level of availability. It depends on third-party providers, and an outage at one of them can interrupt it. We may change or discontinue features.

sections.title: No warranty
sections.body: The Service is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties of any kind, to the fullest extent the law allows. We do not warrant that generated output will be accurate, complete, fit for a particular purpose, or free of errors.

sections.title: Limitation of liability
sections.body: To the fullest extent permitted by law, we are not liable for indirect or consequential losses, lost profits, lost data, or business decisions taken on the basis of anything generated by the Service.

sections.title: Suspension
sections.body: We may suspend or close an account that breaks these terms or puts the Service or its users at risk. You can stop using the Service and delete your account at any time.

sections.title: Governing law
sections.body: These terms are governed by {governingLaw}.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: We may update these terms. Continued use after an update means you accept the revised terms.

cookies.intro: {productName} uses only the cookies it needs to work. There are no advertising cookies, no marketing trackers, and no analytics cookies.

sections.title: What we set
sections.body:
• Authentication and session cookies, set by Supabase. These keep you signed in and are required for the Service to work. Removing them signs you out.
• A language cookie (NEXT_LOCALE), which remembers whether you chose English or Russian.

That is the complete list.

sections.title: Browser storage
sections.body: {productName} also uses your browser's local storage for interface preferences — whether the preview panel is open, whether the navigation is expanded, your language choice, and a short token that lets an unfinished project be resumed. This stays in your browser and is not sent to us as a cookie.

sections.title: What we do not use
sections.body: No analytics cookies. No advertising or retargeting pixels. No third-party trackers. Nothing measures how visitors behave on a project you publish, because {productName} has no such capability.

sections.title: Managing cookies
sections.body: You can clear or block cookies in your browser settings. Blocking the authentication cookies will prevent you from signing in, because the Service cannot keep you signed in without them.

contact.intro: For anything — privacy questions, using the Service, technical support, or account deletion — reach out directly.
contact.responseNote: We try to respond within a reasonable time, but can't yet guarantee an exact response time.

deleteAccount.intro: You can request full deletion of your {productName} account and its associated data at any time.

whatGetsDeleted.title: What gets deleted
whatGetsDeleted.body: Once deletion is confirmed we delete your sign-in account and everything on the server tied to it: your profile, your projects — including the ideas you described, the directions chosen and the generated applications — your conversations with {productName}, your generation history and usage counters, and any versions you published, which stop being reachable at their public address.

whatStays.title: What is not deleted automatically
whatStays.body: Interface preferences kept in your own browser — whether the preview panel is open, your language choice, and the token for resuming an unfinished project. Clear your browser storage to remove them. Technical request logs held by our hosting providers expire on their own retention schedule.

howTo.title: How to request deletion
howTo.body: Account deletion is handled manually — there is no automatic "Delete now" button yet. Email {contactEmail} with the subject "Delete account", from the address linked to your account. We verify that the request comes from the account holder and confirm by email once it is done.

deleteAccount.limitationNote: Note: account deletion isn't instant or fully automated — that's a deliberate choice, so we never delete data by mistake without confirmation.

aiPolicy.intro: {productName} uses AI to help you turn an idea into a working first version. This page explains what that means in practice, and what it does not mean.

sections.title: Where AI is used
sections.body:
• Working out a direction from the idea you describe.
• Generating the first version of your application or site.
• Assisting in the project conversation.

AI runs when you ask for it. {productName} does not generate new versions on its own, does not change a published project without being asked, and does not watch how anyone uses what you published.

sections.title: Which providers
sections.body: {productName} currently sends prompts and project content to Google (Gemini API) and, for parts of the in-project assistant and feedback analysis, to Anthropic. What is sent is described in the Privacy Policy.

sections.title: AI output can be wrong
sections.body: Generated text, code and design are produced by a statistical model. They can contain factual mistakes, broken logic, inaccurate claims, unsuitable wording, or content that does not fit your intent. Output is not reviewed by a human before you see it.

sections.title: Review before you publish
sections.body: You are responsible for what you publish. Read the generated content, check any facts or claims it makes, and confirm it is appropriate for your audience before putting it at a public address. Do not publish generated material that states something you have not verified — particularly anything legal, medical, financial or safety-related.

sections.title: Do not put secrets in prompts
sections.body: Anything you type into a prompt or a project may be sent to an AI provider. Do not include passwords, API keys, payment details, or other people's personal data.

sections.title: No guarantee of outcomes
sections.body: {productName} does not promise that a generated product will attract users, generate revenue, pass a review, or succeed commercially. It produces a working first version to build on; what happens next is your work, not a result the Service guarantees.

sections.title: Limits of the sandbox
sections.body: Generated applications run inside a restricted preview that cannot reach your account or your data. That protects you while previewing. It is not a security review of the generated code, and it does not make the code fit for handling other people's sensitive data.

sections.title: Reporting a problem
sections.body: If generated output is harmful, infringing, or wrong in a way that matters, tell us at {contactEmail}.

refundPolicy.intro: {productName} provides AI-powered tools for creating websites and web applications through subscription plans.

sections.title: Refund Requests
sections.body:
Customers may request a refund within 14 days of their purchase by contacting our support team.

To request a refund, please contact:
{supportEmail}

Please include:
• The email address associated with your {productName} account
• Transaction details
• The reason for your refund request

sections.title: Refund Eligibility
sections.body: Refund requests are reviewed individually. We aim to provide fair resolutions while protecting against abuse of our services.

sections.title: Subscription Cancellation
sections.body: Customers can cancel their subscription at any time. Cancellation prevents future charges but does not automatically issue refunds for previous billing periods unless approved under this policy.

sections.title: Contact
sections.body:
For refund-related questions:
{supportEmail}
